title: Retro-Themed Arcade + Store Opens In Duluth’s Miller Hill Mall - Duluth Country Radio
content: About a month ago, I shared some fun news about a couple of new businesses coming to the Miller Hill Mall in Duluth. Those new businesses include a Vietnamese soup & sandwich shop in the food court, a Mexican eatery called El Azteca Taqueria that just opened, and a new arcade coming to a space near the food court. That arcade is actually part of an expansion of the retailer Mythic Mercantile, which had previously occupied a different space in the mall. When the space where FYE used to be became available, Mythic Mercantile decided to move into the larger space to not only expand their retail offerings of vintage toys, collectibles, and other things of the sort, but also to add a retro-themed arcade too! READ MORE: All Of The Wild New Foods Coming To The Minnesota State Fair This Year The arcade, called "The Warpcore Arcade", just opened recently (along with the new Mythic Mercantile in the same space), so I had to go check it out! When you walk into the space, the arcade is right near the entry, with the Mythic Mercantile retail space behind the arcade. While I didn't count the exact number of machines, there are about 20 different arcade games that span generations. Some of the games include Dance Dance Revolution, Crusi'n World, Tekken, NFL Blitz 99, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Space Invaders, WWF Superstars, along with pinball machines and claw games. For now, the machines are quarter-operated. They are working to get a custom token system online, but in the meantime, bring some quarters (just like the old days!) and get ready to have fun! There are change machines available on-site if you don't have quarters. The staff has a couple of basic rules posted for the arcade. First and foremost, all ages are welcome, but anyone under the age of 14 needs to be accompanied by an adult. No outside food or drinks are allowed, but a selection of candy, pop, and snacks is for sale inside the shop. Speaking of food and drinks, the staff ask that you keep beverages and food on the designated tables and off the games to prevent accidental damage. Finally, the staff just asks for a little respect. First, respect the vintage machines. Don't shake, bang, or rock them around. Be nice to them to keep them running well. Finally, respect each other and the space. Being mindful of others, watching your language, and keeping kids (or energetic adults) from running around or roughhousing. Deeper into the space, behind the arcade, you'll find the retail space of Mythic Mercantile. The shop sells toys and collectibles, action figures, vintage video games and accessories, and plenty of other fun finds that span areas of pop culture and throwback stuff. The arcade and retail store share the same hours, open Thursdays through Sundays, and are closed Mondays, Tuesdays, and Wednesdays. Thursdays through Saturdays, their hours are 11 am until 7 pm, and on Sundays, their hours are 11 am until 6 pm. You can find The Warpcore Arcade and Mythic Mercantile near the food court, right next to Lids and across the hallway from Buckle and Auntie Anne's Pretzels.

title: Here's why shopping in this special, local store is a win-win for vendors and shoppers alike! - allhitskzmk.com
content: The Sierra Vista Food Co-op is more than a place to grab groceries—it’s a community-owned store where everyone is welcome. Sierra Vista Food Co-op Board Member Monica Savarese was a special guest on First Watch visit on 92.3 KWCD. Monica explained that membership is really “more like an ownership.” Being a member supports the shop, but she stressed that everyone is invited to shop there, even if you’re not a member.  “Anyone,” she said, “can stop in for a snack, a specialty item, or a cart full of groceries.” The Sierra Vista Food Co-op serves Sierra Vista and all of Cochise County. According to the Sierra Vista Food Co-op website, the little local grocery was founded in May 2007 and opened its doors in April 2011. It’s organized as a consumer co-op. That means the people who purchase goods and services from the co-op also own the co-op, which keeps profits in our community, rather than a nameless, faceless corporation. Local decisions maximize the service to their members and the Sierra Vista community. It’s difficult to find local farm-to-table produce and cottage goods in Cochise County. According to Monica, the Sierra Vista Food Co-op is one of only two active food co-ops in Arizona. There’s one in Tucson, and another has been working toward opening in Phoenix, but it’s been a long process. For anyone looking for organic, non-GMO, local, and specialty foods, the Sierra Vista Food Co-op is the perfect place. Monica said the store’s purpose is simple: make sure the community has access to “healthy food to support your health journey.” Shelves include produce, grains, pasta, cheeses, non-dairy and vegan options, bulk herbs and spices, local coffee, artisan goods, and foods for special diets, like gluten-free, keto, vegan, plant-based, and other health needs. READ THIS: Harvesting Mesquite Beans: A Guide For Arizona Locals The co-op isn’t a giant, sterile warehouse. It’s a local nook with a little bit of everything, carrying items important to our community but often difficult to find elsewhere. Shopping at the co-op is like voting with your dollars; it keeps more money circulating close to home. Monica told First Watch that the store buys locally when possible and gives local vendors the strongest margin it can for their locally grown and locally made items. They do their best to give local vendors “the biggest margin possible” on their goods. That means a purchase helps support nearby farmers, ranchers, makers, and small businesses. The co-op offers regular member discounts. A few include 20% off special orders, a 10% Wellness Wednesday discount, and a 15% discount on Customer Appreciation Days, plus military and first responder discounts, and more. The discounts don’t apply to locally sourced items from growers and vendors, but they apply to nearly everything else in the store. RELATED: Apple Annie's: Arizona's Perfect Autumn Adventure What makes the co-op special is its neighborly feel. Monica summed it up best: “We’re here for you…whatever you need.” Whether you are trying a pinch of bulk spice, ordering a case of gluten-free oats, or looking for better options for your health journey, the Sierra Vista Food Co-op makes healthy shopping feel personal. You can learn more about the Sierra Vista Food Co-op on its website or Facebook page, or stop by 96 Carmichael Avenue in Sierra Vista.

title: Big Grocery News: Town & Country Is Coming to the Heights - kbulnewstalk.com
content: Great news for grocery shoppers in Billings' Heights. Town & Country Foods will be opening its second Billings location at 1515 Main Street, in the space formerly occupied by Big Lots. The makeover is expected to begin soon, said Town & Country Foods president, Travis Frandsen. Read More: Billings Porta Pot Vandalism Costs Family Business $13K Like most folks in Billings, I shop around. For some things (or if I'm in a hurry), I shop at Albertson's. If we're buying a cartload of stuff and need dog food, toilet paper, and random household goods, it's usually Walmart or Costco. Sometimes I'll hit up Winco, and lately I've been considering getting a Sam's Club membership. Talk about local... Town & Country Foods was founded in Livingston, MT, in 1966. Over the years, the company has expanded with locations across the state. You'll find its stores in Bozeman, Belgrade, Dillon, Lewistown, Billings, and Helena. The new Town & Country store in the Heights will encompass roughly 30,000 square feet, slightly larger than the Grand Avenue store. Langlas & Associates is the general contractor on the project. Frandsen said they are hoping to hire up to 100 employees. Since the company is Employee Owned, he said they prefer hiring full-timers and filling in with part-time employees as needed. I've found lots of Montana products at Town & Country Foods, including Wheat Montana Products, Farver Farms products, and their meat case featured delicious cuts from Marbled Beef, a ranch near Billings.

title: Rocker Bad Back Golf Outing Raises Record $5,400 For W. Michigan Cancer Center At Shamrock Hills - 1077 WRKR
content: Members of the community gathered at the Shamrock Hills Golf Club in Gobles, Michigan, for the Rocker Bad Back golf outing, and we raised nearly $ 5,400 for the W. Michigan Cancer Center. This is the most that we’ve ever been able to raise for W. Michigan Cancer Center in one event, and it was a day filled with fun, mostly perfect weather, and a whole bunch of shenanigans. Bronson Healthcare stepped up in a big way, becoming the title sponsor for the event, along with McDonald’s Towing, which brought one of the brand-new tow trucks that literally had all the bells and whistles and put it on display in the parking lot. Volcano Pizza was also present for the Caddyshack hole; we golfers had a chance of winning a gopher club cover and snagging an easier hole in one. Golfers also delighted in attempting to sync their putt a little differently, tossing a giant inflatable golf ball into large solo cups for an enlarged impromptu beer pong. It was all capped off at the end of the day with trophies awarded to the winners, beach, bums, runners-up, and the team with the most strokes, all crafted by Dr. Hooks in Kalamazoo. With every ticket that was purchased for the golf outing, money was donated to W. Michigan Cancer Center, and along with all of our sponsors, 50-50, silent auction, and other fun activities, we were able to raise nearly $5400, which will help go towards treatment and many other services provided by the center. We are eyeing the same date next year at Shamrock Hills Golf Club, Friday, July 9, for our next Rocker Bad Back Golf Outing.

Wei reportedly told shareholders at the annual meeting in Taiwan that AI chip demand will outpace supply for years to come, even as one of the world's biggest chipmakers races to expand its manufacturing footprint. Wei's commentary hinted that production capacity is one of the bottlenecks at a time when hyperscalers and chip companies are investing heavily to build AI infrastructure. According to a Bloomberg report, Wei said the company will not be able to meet demand from its American customers even after its manufacturing facilities become operational in the U.S. At the time of writing, TSM stock was down over 2% premarket on Thursday. In an earnings call post the Q1 announcement, company management stated that it had acquired two land parcels in Arizona to build additional fabs and meet multiyear demand from its U.S. customers. Later in April, according to a Reuters report, the company management said that it plans to open a chip packaging facility by 2029. Despite the supply-demand gap, Wei added that TSMC will refrain from suddenly increasing prices to maintain a stable business, the report stated. However, Wei reportedly added that it will be a long time before the company can meet customer demand. Major hyperscalers are set to spend billions on AI infrastructure this year alone, and TSMC produces the majority of the world's advanced AI chips. As a part of the U.S.-Taiwan trade pact, TSMC envisions building at least four more US chipmaking plants on top of six already planned, a total of 10 facilities entailing $165 billion in announced investments plus roughly $100 billion in additional capital, according to the report. Two plots of land acquired in Arizona should be enough to satisfy TSMC's needs for a decade, Wei said. The expansion is critical as TSMC is essential for Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs, AMD's MI450/Helios chips, and custom ASICs from Broadcom and others. The company raised its full-year sales guidance in April and said capital spending should trend toward the upper end of its $56 billion forecast range. "With a target of 10K Starship launches per year and aggressive capacity increases on communications/AI infrastructure, the company will dominate the fastest-growing industry over the next century," Oppenheimer said. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang pushed back on growing speculation that the bellwether’s dominance in AI compute is vulnerable to rival Google’s TPUs and Amazon’s Trainium chips or others. He argued that building something meaningfully better than Nvidia is “not that easy”. In a wide-ranging conversation with Dwarkesh Patel, when asked whether rival AI chips could erode Nvidia’s moat, he explained that AI infrastructure goes beyond just raw computing. He argued that the company’s strength comes from its role as a middle layer in a complex ecosystem that spans TSMC and Micron, among others, as suppliers, and downstream hyperscalers running AI workloads. And this business model makes it harder for competitors to replicate. “Look at the number of ASICs [application-specific integrated circuits] that have been canceled. Just because you’re going to build an ASIC… You still have to build something better than Nvidia. It’s not that easy building something better than Nvidia. It’s not sensible, actually,” Huang said. In his words, it is about converting AI “electrons-to-tokens,” which requires deep engineering across layers rather than focusing on designing a faster chip. "Nvidia's computing stack is the best performance per TCO [total cost of ownership] in the world, bar none,” Huang said, adding that InferenceMAX, the open-source, nightly-updated AI inference benchmarking framework, backed his claims about Nvidia's superiority over Google's TPUs or Amazon's Trainium chips. “I'm not offended by other people using something else and trying things. If they don't try these other things, how would they know how good ours is?” He also pushed back against the idea that Alphabet-owned Google’s TPUs or Amazon’s Trainium chips could replace Nvidia at scale. Huang said that while these chips were specialized, Nvidia’s GPUs were flexible, allowing developers to experiment with new AI models and algorithms, and were available across major clouds, giving them a massive reach across customers. AI infrastructure spending continues to surge across Big Tech, with demand still heavily anchored to Nvidia’s chips even as alternatives emerge. Huang’s comments come at a time when Anthropic has deepened its ties with Google, while also working with Amazon. title: Fast Food Store in Northern Colorado Still Closed - Fort Collins Country Radio
content: There are many fast-food options in Northern Colorado, but most people have their preferred places to go. Most enjoy going to locations that are closest to their home, on their way to work, or near a store they often visit. When one of these places closes, it forces customers to call an audible, go to a different location, or stop eating there altogether. One popular fast food chain has had a location closed for months in Northern Colorado, and many are wondering when it will reopen. Back in May, the McDonald's located at 1273 Grand Market Ave in Berthoud closed. It has remained closed since, and many are left wondering when and if it will reopen. While caution tape surrounds the building and it looks like construction or a remodel is being done, very little has happened since the closure, and there are no machines or crews spotted around the building most days. Some speculated that the store could open on July 8, but that will not happen, as there is still plenty of work to be done. On the door, there is a sign that reads, 'The store will be closed for maintenance repairs until further notice. Sorry for the inconvenience. ' So what exactly are they doing? As seen in the picture above, there is a sign that reads, ‘Uneven Surface,' and if you walk around the McDonald's in Berthoud, you will notice plenty of cracks and that the parking lot and sidewalk are uneven. The ground is uneven and needs to be taken care of before the store can reopen, and it looks like the fast food chain still has a ways to go before opening once again. With the foundation in question, could the businesses around the McDonald's close soon for the same reason? It is unknown how long the fast food chain will remain closed, but after a couple of months and little progress made, it won't be this week, or even perhaps this month.

title: TSMC Outpaces Sector & Peers in a Year: Is the Stock Still a Buy? - The Globe and Mail
content: The global semiconductor foundry market is attracting growing investor interest, driven by advancements in artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning, 5G and the Internet of Things (IoT). Foundries continue to heavily invest in research and development to offer advanced process nodes, helping meet demand for these high-tech applications. According to Fortune Business Insights, the market is projected to witness a CAGR of 3.4% through 2026-2034, expanding from $175.1 billion in 2025. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing CompanyTSM, or TSMC, dominates this space with more than 70% market share. Over the past year, the stock has surged 90.4%, outperforming the Zacks Computer and Technology sector’s 37.2% gain and the S&P 500 composite’s 24.9% return. TSMC also outpaced peers GlobalFoundriesGFS and ON Semiconductor ON, or onsemi, both of which gained 58.9% over the same period. Based on its last closing price, TSM stock is trading above its 50-day and 200-day simple moving averages (SMAs), signaling sustained bullish momentum. TSMC reported May 2026 consolidated net revenues of NT$416.98 billion (New Taiwan Dollars), up 1.5% from April 2026 and 30.1% from May 2025. For the first five months of 2026, consolidated revenues totaled NT$1.96 trillion, marking a 30% increase compared with the same period last year. Robust AI-related demand underpins the company’s growth outlook. Management stated that the shift from generative AI and the query mode to agentic AI and command and action mode is driving higher token consumption and increasing the need for computation, supporting demand for leading-edge silicon. TSMC continues to see a strong signal and positive outlook from its customers as well as cloud service providers, maintaining a high level of conviction in the multiyear AI megatrend. Performance-wise, first-quarter 2026 revenues increased 6.4% sequentially to $35.9 billion, slightly ahead of the company’s guidance. Gross margin expanded by 390 basis points (bps) sequentially to 66.2%, driven by cost improvement efforts, a higher overall capacity utilization rate and a more favorable foreign exchange rate. Operating margin improved 410 bps sequentially to 58.1% due to operating leverage. TSMC’s 2-nanometer (N2) and A16 technologies continue to lead the industry in addressing the demand for energy-efficient computing, with almost all the innovators working with TSMC. N2 is ramping up successfully in multiple phases at both the company’s Hsinchu and Kaohsiung sites, led by strong demand from both smartphone and High-Performance Computing (“HPC”) AI applications. At the same time, the company is stepping up its capital expenditure to expand its global 3-nanometer capacity. The expansion spans Taiwan, Arizona and Japan, alongside 5-nanometer tool conversions and capacity optimization across N7, N5 and N3 nodes. TSMC’s A14 technology development is also on track, for which it is seeing a high level of customer interest and engagement from both smartphone and HPC applications. TSMC remains confident that full-year 2026 revenues will grow by more than 30% in U.S. dollar terms, reflecting the strength of its differentiated technology and broad customer base. For the second quarter, the company expects revenues between $39 billion and $40.2 billion, representing 10% sequential growth and 32% year-over-year growth at the midpoint. Based on an exchange rate assumption of $1 to 31.7 New Taiwan Dollars, the second-quarter gross margin is projected at 65.5%-67.5% and operating margin at 56.5%-58.5%. Management noted that the initial ramp-up of its 2-nanometer technology will dilute gross margin by 2%-3% for the year. TSMC also expects capital expenditures to trend toward the high end of its previously announced $52-$56 billion range as it expands capacity to support customer demand. Despite the elevated spending, management reiterated its focus on delivering profitable growth for shareholders. At present, the Zacks Consensus Estimate expects TSMC’s earnings per share (EPS) to grow 44.1% to $15.35 in 2026, followed by another 27% increase to $19.50 in 2027. Analyst estimates for both years have moved higher over the past three months. The company’s revenues are expected to grow 32.3% in 2026 and another 26.6% in 2027. Based on the forward 12-month Price/Earnings (P/E), TSM trades at 25.84X, slightly above its median of 24.33X and the 24.98X sector average. In contrast, GFS trades at a P/E of 38.63X, while ON sits with 24.35X. TSMC benefits from strong demand for its leading-edge process technologies. The performance of its key profitability metrics is supported by cost improvement efforts and a high-capacity utilization rate. The higher level of capital spending reflects management’s confidence in delivering profitable growth to shareholders and also capturing long-term growth opportunities. At the same time, TSMC remains well-positioned to continue capitalizing on the strong industry tailwinds. The stock has significantly outperformed the sector and other peers over the past 12 months. From a valuation standpoint, TSM is trading close to both its historical median and sector average. Backed by positive earnings estimate revisions, the stock appears to be an attractive investment opportunity. TSM carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy) at present. Zhitong Finance APP learned that Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM.US), the global leader in wafer foundry services, will hold its second-quarter 2026 analyst conference on July 16. According to a research report released by GF Securities, Taiwan Semiconductor is expected to raise its full-year earnings guidance at that time and simultaneously increase its capital expenditure plan for 2027. In a report, Guangfa Securities analyst Jeff Pu noted that AI accelerators and CPUs continue to drive advanced-node utilization rates (UTR) to remain at high levels, while the trend of ever-increasing on-chip memory capacity—unmatched by process scaling—also provides support. Notably, Taiwan Semiconductor's capital expenditure acceleration began in 2025, lagging behind the onset of the AI demand cycle by roughly 1.5 to 2 years, which implies that some market share erosion or demand spillover is inevitable. Consequently, it is expected that Taiwan Semiconductor may further accelerate capacity expansion for its N5, N3, and N2 nodes in the second half of 2027, complemented by strategic pricing adjustments. Guangfa Securities reiterated its "Buy" rating on Taiwan Semiconductor and raised the target price from NT$2,808 to NT$2,900. At the same time, the firm increased its 2026 and 2027 earnings per share (EPS) forecasts for Taiwan Semiconductor by 3% and 12%, respectively. On the financial front, Jeff Pu forecasts second-quarter revenue to grow approximately 11% quarter over quarter (the company's guidance midpoint is a 10% QoQ increase), with a gross margin of around 68% (the company's guidance range is 65.5%–67.5%, while the Bloomberg consensus estimate stands at 67%, revised upward to 69%–70%). Third-quarter revenue is expected to grow 13% quarter over quarter (vs. the consensus estimate of 9%), while gross margin is forecast to edge down slightly to 67.1% (compared with the consensus of 65.8%). Full-year guidance may be revised further upward from the current "year-over-year growth exceeding 30%." On the capital expenditure front, GF Securities forecasts that Taiwan Semiconductor's total capital spending will reach US$56 billion in 2026 and further climb to US$73 billion in 2027. However, supply bottlenecks for extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography equipment may to some extent constrain the actual implementation of capital expenditures and equipment procurement. In terms of market consensus, analysts currently forecast Taiwan Semiconductor's adjusted EPS for the second quarter at $3.83 and its revenue at $39.32 billion.
